name: Wright’s evolutionary population genetics
description: Wright analyzed how selection, migration, chance and population structure can jointly affect inherited variation.

date.basis: Year of the dated publication, or a broad historian-estimated composition interval; no first discovery claimed.

events.statement: Wright published Evolution in Mendelian Populations in 1931.

evidence.supports: The 1931 paper examines Mendelian equilibrium, selection, migration and random fluctuations in finite populations.
Wright retrospectively described his mathematical synthesis and acknowledged other theorists.
The 1931 paper examines Mendelian equilibrium, selection, migration and random fluctuations in finite populations.

earliest_record.rationale: Dated witness within the inspected evidence; not a global-priority claim.

caveats: Wright was one of several founders of mathematical population genetics. The paper presents idealized models; the reach of his shifting-balance scenario in nature remains debated.
